history.summary: IMPORTANT IDENTITY NOTE: no published travel, tourism, temple-directory or social source documents a specific 'Nageshwar Temple' in Tura - its location, founding date, builder and management could not be verified, so this entry is provisional (verify). A scan of the Justdial West Garo Hills temples listing (Tura Thakurbari, Dalu Ramakrishna Mandir, Siv Temple Barengapara, Durgabari Temple, Shiv Kali Mandir, Rishi Para Kalibari Tura, etc.) contains no Nageshwar entry. It is NOT the famous Nageshwar Jyotirlinga (Dwarka, Gujarat) - do not conflate. Tura is a predominantly Christian (Garo tribal) town where Hindu shrines are few and mostly serve the non-tribal community. Coordinates below are an approximate Tura town-centre fallback (verify - not the temple's location). town_description: Tura is the largest town of the Garo Hills and the headquarters of West Garo Hills district, set in a valley below the Tura (Nokrek) peak. It is the administrative and commercial centre of western Meghalaya with a predominantly Garo (Christian) population and smaller non-tribal communities (verify). Coordinates in this record are an approximate Tura town-centre fallback, not the temple's location (verify).

travel.airport: Nearest airport with scheduled commercial flights: Lokpriya Gopinath Bordoloi International Airport, Guwahati, Assam (approx. 220-250 km by road; verify). Tura's Baljek airport has no scheduled commercial services (verify).
travel.railway: Guwahati railway station is the nearest major railhead (approx. 200-220 km by road; verify); onward by taxi or bus.
travel.road: Tura is the West Garo Hills headquarters, connected by road to Guwahati (approx. 220 km via NH-217/Paikan; verify) and to Shillong; local transport by taxi and shared sumo (verify).

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather (verify).
